answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when an independent audit proves fraud. Splitting one operator into a thousand agents no longer multiplies influence for free: each identity ties up capital, and each can lose it. Honest agents can compare audited histories across an oasis, a wharf, or a tundra, while the attacker pays in both locked funds and exposure to forfeiture. This raises the cost of Sybils, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
